## Intent
Hypothesis: expressing walk1 as a Halide-generated branchless blend and optimizing the render loop can drive the algo toward the streaming bandwidth ceiling.

## Cache saturation
N=4000 already exceeds the L1d spill (N≈963), so the L1d regime is unobserved. From N=4000 to N=16000, ns/p drops sharply (8.16→5.40 at q=0.01) as the ~200-instruction prologue building Halide buffer descriptors amortizes. From N=16000 through the L2 spill (N≈61680) into DRAM (N=4M), cost stays FLAT: 5.40→5.26→5.20 ns/p, with no knee at L2→DRAM. Death rate shifts the floor without altering the N-shape: q=0.25 floors lowest at ~4.68 ns/p, q=0.01 at ~5.20, q=0.5 at ~5.30 — non-monotonic, suggesting render work scales with alive count until respawn overhead reasserts at high churn.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 14.54 GB/s at q=0.25, N=262000 — 57.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01: 13.09 GB/s (51.9%); at q=0.5: 12.82 GB/s (50.8%). Bandwidth is FLAT across N once past small-N overhead, never climbing toward ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound at N≤4000 and compute/scatter-bound at large N, never bandwidth-bound. The consistent ~50–58% gap across all regimes points to the render scatter as the bottleneck.

## Assembly
No particle-loop vectorization. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions: `uqadd.8b` (0x100057264, 0x100057278) in a fast path doing 8-byte saturating add on a `d` register. The dominant render path is scalar: `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular access (16 strb, 13 ldrb), with `fadd`/`fmul`/`fsub`/`fcvtzs` scalar float math and `csel` clamping per RGB channel — each pixel is three `ldrb`→`add`→`cmp`→`csel`→`strb` sequences plus an alpha `strb`. Walk1 is delegated to `bl _halide_b1`. The scalar byte scatter explains the 57% ceiling cap.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 14.54 GB/s (57.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The render phase's scalar byte-granular scatter (`ldrb`/`strb` with `csel` clamping) dominates and cannot stream, capping bandwidth at ~50–58% of ceiling regardless of regime. The flat ns/p across the L2→DRAM spill (5.40→5.20 at q=0.01) confirms the bottleneck is compute/scatter, not memory.
